topic: sequential automatic mixing, live predictive gain control, bleed robustness, and mix evaluation

source_cards.title: Rethinking Automatic Music Mixing as Sequential Stem Blending
source_cards.limited_conclusion: A fixed submix can serve as an acoustic anchor while only the incoming stem is adapted; input order is a testable control variable, not a universal hierarchy.
limitations: early sparse submix states not represented by degradation synthesis
not SOTA on tonal-balance and style-similarity metrics

source_cards.title: AILive Mixer: A Deep Learning based Zero Latency Automatic Music Mixer for Live Music Performances
source_cards.limited_conclusion: Past-context prediction can remove an audio lookahead buffer for 50-ms mono-gain frames, but entrances, gain discontinuities, clipping and synthetic-to-real bleed shift require explicit safety tests.
limitations: no significant evidence separating ALM-MR from ALM-SR

source_cards.title: The Mix Evaluation Dataset
source_cards.limited_conclusion: Blind preference, technical quality and structured instrument-specific comments should be retained as distinct observations.
limitations: current raw-track access and per-track licenses not reverified
abstract says 180 mixes while the paper table reports 181

knowledge_cards.title: Acoustic anchor
knowledge_cards.claim: A fixed accepted submix constrains the next stem decision without rewriting prior context.

knowledge_cards.title: Order is a control
knowledge_cards.claim: Stem order changes sequential results and must be conditioned by section role.

knowledge_cards.title: Raw can win
knowledge_cards.claim: Automatic processing can degrade an already suitable stem; no-processing and level-only are required baselines.

knowledge_cards.title: Metrics can disagree
knowledge_cards.claim: Tonal-balance or crest distribution distance can disagree with listener preference.

knowledge_cards.title: Predictive zero latency
knowledge_cards.claim: Zero audio-lookahead can be implemented by next-frame prediction and remains fallible at unexpected entrances.

knowledge_cards.title: Temporal safety
knowledge_cards.claim: Learned live gain trajectories require explicit step, slew, recovery and clipping tests.

knowledge_cards.title: Bleed domain gap
knowledge_cards.claim: An isolated-track target is not ground truth for a naturally bleeding live stage.

knowledge_cards.title: Preference is not quality
knowledge_cards.claim: Preference, technical quality and instrument-specific comments are distinct evaluation fields.

rule_candidates.when_apply: adding one instrument or role into an accepted submix
rule_candidates.change: process only the incoming stem while holding the accepted submix fixed
rule_candidates.proposed_range: workflow constraint; no numeric DSP range
rule_candidates.verify: null/context comparison plus loudness-matched blind A/B
rule_candidates.cancel: the defect is located in the existing submix rather than the incoming stem

rule_candidates.instrument_section: whole mix; section roles; no automatic vocal priority
rule_candidates.change: compare foundation-first, section-role priority, and counterbalanced/random control; include rhythm-guitar foundation for Premiera
rule_candidates.range_origin: project experiment design; the paper compared domain and random orders
rule_candidates.verify: intermediate renders and final loudness-matched blind preference
rule_candidates.cancel: order effects do not repeat across sections or worsen protected qualities

rule_candidates.when_apply: before applying automatic processing to any stem
rule_candidates.proposed_range: level grid determined per loudness-matched experiment
rule_candidates.range_origin: project control requirement supported by raw-mix results
rule_candidates.verify: processed candidate must beat both baselines in blind comparison
rule_candidates.cancel: no reliable advantage over either baseline

rule_candidates.change: store and evaluate intermediate submix before continuing
rule_candidates.range_origin: sequential model provides intermediate outputs; cadence is workflow design
rule_candidates.verify: structured preference and technical comments at intermediate and final stages
rule_candidates.cancel: later corrections systematically compensate earlier harm

rule_candidates.instrument_section: live multitrack, especially percussion and sudden entrances
rule_candidates.change: enforce tested gain-step/slew bounds, hysteresis or equivalent smoothing, confidence and safe fallback
rule_candidates.proposed_range: not specified; derive from onset-test grid
rule_candidates.range_origin: engineering hypothesis from reported gain jumps, not a paper parameter prescription
rule_candidates.verify: first-event error, max gain step, clipping, recovery and blind A/B
rule_candidates.cancel: smoothing masks attacks or predictor is less stable than static/level-only baseline

rule_candidates.instrument_section: entrances, returns after silence, fills and accents
rule_candidates.change: include explicit onset and re-entry cases
rule_candidates.proposed_range: 50-ms prediction horizon as tested in the paper plus project-designed controls
rule_candidates.range_origin: paper architecture and project experiment design
rule_candidates.cancel: first events are systematically lost or gain jumps increase

rule_candidates.instrument_section: full live mix and representative sections
rule_candidates.change: run separate operational non-normalized and loudness-matched blind preference tests
rule_candidates.range_origin: project design responding to the unnormalized live paper and preference-quality distinction
rule_candidates.verify: report clipping/headroom separately from preference and technical-quality scores
rule_candidates.cancel: conclusions still depend on uncontrolled level differences
